newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China Zhuzhou smelter to cut 1997 lead production.
newsitem.headline: China Zhuzhou smelter to cut 1997 lead production.

text.p: China's Zhuzhou smelter, one of the country's largest for lead and zinc, would cut its production of lead by 20,000 tonnes to 70,000 tonnes in 1997, a senior smelter official said on Tuesday.
"We will decrease our production of electrolytic lead from 90,000 in 1996 to 70,000 this year," the smelter's director of technical development Shu Yuzhang told Reuters.
"Last year was a good year for lead, this year is bad," Shu said in Hong Kong while attending a week-long China non-ferrous metals fair.
"Lead prices in China have dropped from 7,000 yuan ($843) late last year to about 6,500 yuan ($783) now," Shu said.
Of the 70,000 tonnes of lead to be produced in 1997, about 40,000-50,000 tonnes would be exported, Shu said.
Weak international prices would mean fewer exports, Shu said, noting that world prices above $700 per tonne would be favorable.
"If people offer $720 FOB China for lead, then we can do something," another source at Zhuzhou said.
